paper.title_en: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
paper.abstract_en: The analytical modeling of a plasma wakefield driven by a relativistic proton beam is an element in optimizing advanced plasma-based acceleration schemes. In this work, we present a 1D nonlinear fluid framework under the quasi-static approximation to describe the wake potential excited by a positively charged proton driver which attracts background electrons into a density compression rather than expelling them. We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using a two-bunch scheme, our piecewise-event integration model is validated to high numerical accuracy ($\sim 10^{-11}~\mathrm{GV/m}$) against independent phase-space quadrature of cold-fluid solutions, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ ramped micro-bunch train with fixed $2π$ spacing, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a piecewise analytical scaling model. This formulation maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic post-train residual wake plateau, which is determined exactly by the conserved vacuum Hamiltonian invariant evaluated at the final bunch-train exit state. Furthermore, the framework estimates the onset of nonlinear phase-slippage that arrests growth and causes the transient wakefield overshoot to decay toward the residual horizon. Providing immediate 1D analytical benchmarks, this computationally inexpensive tool offers a reproducible baseline for verifying 1D fluid and multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) codes. It also provides a tractable starting point for exploring asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles relevant to transformer-ratio optimization.
